academic_terms: indistinguishability of real and ideal views
industry_terms: privacy of the prover's secret inputs

descriptions.semantic: An interaction or proof string for a true statement reveals nothing about the prover's secret witness beyond the statement's truth. Formally there exists an efficient simulator that, given only the public statement (no witness), produces a transcript computationally indistinguishable from a real prover-verifier interaction. Anything an adversarial verifier could learn from the real proof, it could have computed itself from the statement alone.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A relation between TWO systems — the real prover-verifier composition and an ideal simulator composition — required to be observationally indistinguishable to any efficient distinguisher. It is therefore a property of the *pair* of behaviour distributions, not of any single execution: a hyperproperty (non-interference between the secret-witness input channel and the verifier-observable output channel).
descriptions.security: Confidentiality of the secret inputs. Its violation is a witness-leakage / information-flow breach: a verifier (or chain observer) extracts secret data — keys, balances, identities, preimages — from proofs that were supposed to hide them. Distinct from soundness violations, which are integrity breaches (false statements accepted).
descriptions.execution_semantics: At the system level it manifests as: chosen public inputs/outputs, Fiat-Shamir transcript construction, randomness (blinding) usage, and which signals of a circuit are exposed. Leakage occurs when randomness is reused or insufficient, when public outputs are a non-trivial function of the witness, when the simulator's required trapdoor/CRS assumptions fail, or when side channels (timing, proof size variation) correlate with the witness.
descriptions.formal_verification: NOT a trace property; single-trace symbolic execution and fuzzing are categorically inapplicable to the privacy claim. Establishing ZK is a cryptographic reduction: exhibit a PPT simulator and prove indistinguishability under stated hardness assumptions — pen-and-paper or mechanized in a relational/probabilistic proof assistant (EasyCrypt). Circuit tools instead target the SEPARABLE, single-system sub-properties (soundness via under-constraint detection), which is where real-world bugs cluster.

formalization.signature: Relation R subset Statements x Witnesses. Interactive system (P,V) for language L_R = { x : exists w . (x,w) in R }. View_{V*}<P(w),V*>(x) = the random variable of V*'s entire view (its coins + received messages). ~_c denotes computational indistinguishability of distribution ensembles.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Completeness:  forall (x,w) in R . Pr[ <P(w),V>(x) = accept ] >= 1 - negl(|x|).
Knowledge soundness (the INTEGRITY dual, see relationships):  exists PPT extractor E . forall P* . Pr[<P*,V>(x)=accept] = eps  =>  Pr[ (x, E^{P*}(x)) in R ] >= poly-related-to(eps) - negl.

temporal_logic.ltl: n/a — ZK is not a temporal trace property; do not encode it in LTL/CTL. Attempting to is the category error this record exists to flag.

formalization.state_machine: Two LTS instances are compared: M_real (P with secret w composed with V*) and M_ideal (Sim with only x). The 2-safety / observational requirement: for the witness-input low-equivalence relation, the verifier-observable outputs are indistinguishable. Self-composition reduces the hyperproperty to a safety property on the product machine M_real x M_ideal — the standard route to mechanizing k-safety.
formalization.type_theoretic: Non-interference in an information-flow type system: label the witness High and the public statement/transcript Low; ZK is the typing judgment that no High input flows to a Low-observable output beyond the declassification permitted by membership in L_R. The declassification policy is exactly 'x in L_R'.
formalization.hyperproperty: ZK is a 2-execution property (compare real vs. ideal) and is verified either by (a) cryptographic reduction with an explicit simulator, or (b) for the information-flow fragment, by self-composition + a safety checker on the product system. It lives in the hypersafety class of the Clarkson-Schneider lattice; the *privacy* part is not expressible as a set of admissible single traces.

relationships.note: Tension with public-auditability/transparency requirements; resolved by selective disclosure, not by weakening ZK.
Composes with Knowledge-Soundness (the integrity dual): a proof system needs BOTH; they are independent and a system can have one without the other.
Refined at the circuit level into per-circuit non-leakage of exposed signals.
Relies on hardness assumptions (DLOG/DDH/knowledge-of-exponent/AGM, or hash-as-RO for Fiat-Shamir) and, for NIZK, a correctly-generated CRS / no toxic-waste leak.

attack_surface.pattern: reused or low-entropy prover randomness lets the verifier solve for the witness across proofs
attack_surface.notes: Distinct mechanism, same flavour: randomness reuse collapses the simulator's hiding.

attack_surface.pattern: a public signal is a non-trivial / invertible function of the secret witness
attack_surface.notes: Circuit-level: audit the map from witness to public inputs for injectivity/leakage.

attack_surface.pattern: transcript hashing omits a value, enabling grinding or revealing structure (weak Fiat-Shamir)
incident_refs: 'Frozen Heart' weak-Fiat-Shamir vulnerability class — VERIFY scope before citing
attack_surface.notes: Primarily a SOUNDNESS issue but can interact with the privacy argument's RO assumption.

attack_surface.pattern: trusted-setup CRS secret retained, breaking the simulation/extraction assumptions
proof generation timing/size correlates with witness
attack_surface.notes: Outside the idealized model; requires constant-time prover.

metrics: mutual information between public signals and witness (audit-time, on synthetic witnesses)
invariant_checkpoints: every exposed public signal is provably independent of the secret part of the witness (declassification-policy check)
runtime_assertions: n/a on-chain: ZK is not observable from a single transcript; it is a property of the SYSTEM, not of any one proof
telemetry: randomness-source health monitoring on the proving infrastructure

strategies.notes: Mechanize the game-hopping indistinguishability proof under explicit assumptions. This is the only thing that actually establishes the privacy claim.

tools: self-composition + Halmos/SMT on the witness->public-signal map
strategies.notes: Targets the non-leakage fragment, not the full cryptographic claim.

strategies.approach: Circuit SOUNDNESS analysis (the dual, BPO:0070 — included because it is what tooling actually does)
strategies.notes: CRITICAL CLARIFICATION: these tools find UNDER-CONSTRAINT (soundness/integrity) bugs — the dominant real-world circuit failure — they do NOT verify the ZK/privacy property. Conflating the two is a common and dangerous mistake.

testability: privacy is not unit-testable; test the separable invariants: public-signal independence on randomized witnesses, prover randomness entropy, constant-time proving

static: information-flow typing of circuit signals (High witness vs Low public)
audit map witness -> public inputs for leakage
design_patterns: audited/MPC trusted-setup ceremony or transparent setup (STARK/FRI) to remove toxic-waste
strong Fiat-Shamir: hash the full transcript including all public data

assumptions.statement: Underlying hardness assumption holds (e.g. DLOG/DDH/knowledge-of-exponent in AGM, or random-oracle for the hash in Fiat-Shamir).
For NIZK with trusted setup, the CRS secret ('toxic waste') was destroyed; at least one ceremony participant was honest.
Prover implementation matches the proven abstract protocol (no implementation-level side channel or randomness defect).

provenance.notes: This record's primary pedagogical role in BPO is to make the trace-property / hyperproperty boundary concrete and to separate the privacy claim (ZK, needs reduction) from the integrity claim (soundness/under-constraint, where automated tooling lives).
